planting.note: Pot up offsets or nursery starts in spring once nights stay above 45F in a fast-draining cactus mix.

directions: This Mexican native forms a broad, flattened rosette of thick, powdery, silvery-lavender leaves that give it a ghostly, almost metallic sheen. Grow in bright full sun to intensify the pale coloring, since low light causes the rosette to stretch and lose its dense, chalky bloom. Plant in gritty, fast-draining cactus mix and water only after the soil dries completely, keeping water off the leaves to preserve the delicate powder coating. It is a common breeding parent for pastel hybrid echeverias and tolerates brief light frost if kept dry.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Root stem cuttings or pot up nursery starts in spring in bright light and gritty succulent soil.

directions: Known as the Woolly Rose for its dense coat of fine white hairs covering thick green leaves tipped in red, this hybrid (E. setosa x E. pulvinata) forms a shrubby clump of fuzzy rosettes on short stems. Give it full sun to bright light to keep the rosette compact and the wool dense; too little light causes stretching and thin, sparse hairs. Plant in fast-draining cactus mix and water deeply but infrequently, letting the soil dry fully between waterings since the woolly leaves are prone to rot if kept damp. Older plants branch and mound, making an attractive textured accent in dish gardens.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Divide offsets or pot nursery starts in spring in gritty, fast-draining succulent mix.

directions: This compact hybrid produces tight rosettes of pale, translucent green leaves with thin, crystalline red-pink margins that intensify in cool weather and bright light. Grow in full sun to bring out the icy edge coloring; in shade the leaves stay flat green and the rosette loosens. Use a fast-draining cactus and succulent mix and water only once the soil is fully dry, since the fleshy leaves rot quickly in soggy conditions. It offsets readily around the base, making it easy to propagate and fill out a container over a season or two.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

planting.note: Divide offsets in spring and pot in a shallow container with fast-draining succulent mix.

directions: A selected cultivar of the classic zebra haworthia, Big Band shows broader, more pronounced white horizontal bands and pearly warty ridges across thick, dark green pointed leaves than the standard species. Grow in bright indirect light or partial shade, since direct hot sun can bleach or scorch the leaves while too little light dulls the banding. Plant in a shallow pot with gritty, fast-draining succulent soil and water only when the soil has dried out, as this compact rosette is sensitive to overwatering and root rot. It stays small and clumps readily, making it well suited to dish gardens and windowsill collections.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference
